Sam (support): Heads-up: customer 'customer-app' hit streaming regressions after Python SDK 0.9.2 upgrade. They see SSE disconnects mid-response and partial output printed, then the iterator just stops — no exception. Billing shows token charge for the full response.

customer-app: Repro steps I ran (minimal):
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV['API_KEY'])
async def get():
    async for chunk in client.stream('chat.completions', model='open-llama', messages=[...]):
        print(chunk)
# result: prints first few chunks, then stops. ctrl+c doesn't raise inside the generator.
```
Logs we captured (SSE connection):
```
[2026-02-22T15:03:10.123Z] SSE open id=abc123
[2026-02-22T15:03:10.234Z] data: {"id":"r1","delta":"Hello"}
[2026-02-22T15:03:10.300Z] data: {"id":"r1","delta":" world"}
[2026-02-22T15:03:11.001Z] connection closed code=1006
# client shows no exception, generator silent.
```

Jin (sdk): Thanks, Sam — can you confirm exact SDK version and python runtime? Also please enable REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 and paste the raw SSE frames (we're interested in headers around the disconnect).

customer-app: Running python 3.11.8, sdk 0.9.2. Enabled REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG and here is the raw excerpt: 
```
> GET /v1/stream/chat HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> stream-session-id: sess-7f3a
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Connection: keep-alive
data: {"id":"r1","delta":"Hello"}

data: {"id":"r1","delta":" world"}

# then: TCP FIN from server, no terminator event, no 'event: done' line
```

Mona (sre): I think I saw something similar in a Node customer last week. If the server side closes the TCP connection without an SSE 'done' event, some clients treat that as EOF while others swallow it. That creates a race: our Python iterator's cancellation path was introduced to avoid leaking tasks, but it may swallow EOF when a reconnect path tries to re-attach.

Jin (sdk): Exactly — initial triage: there's a race between the internal _drain_task that reads SSE frames and the async generator close path. If the connection drops and the reconnect logic fires while the consumer has partially consumed the last chunk, the buffer can be dropped and the generator completes silently. That explains the partial print + silent stop and the downstream billing showing full tokens (server finished generation) while client didn't see the final event.

Quick workaround for Python users (apply in user code if you cannot upgrade):
```py
# workaround: wrap the stream iterator so we drain pending frames on close
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
@asynccontextmanager
async def safe_stream(client, *args, **kwargs):
    gen = client.stream(*args, **kwargs)
    try:
        yield gen
    finally:
        # ensure pending frames are consumed or generator closed cleanly
        try:
            await gen.aclose()
        except Exception:
            # swallow to avoid hiding original errors
            pass
```
# usage:
async with safe_stream(client, 'chat.completions', model='open-llama', messages=...) as g:
    async for chunk in g:
        print(chunk)
```
This forces the generator close and reduces the chance of silent buffer drop. It's not ideal; we'll patch the SDK.

Ellie (prod-eng): Billing note: if server completes and charges, but client didn't receive final tokens, customers will understandably escalate. We should add server-side dedupe via 'stream-session-id' header and recommend clients set it to a UUID per logical request. Also add a visible metric to Console: 'partial_streams' and token_dedupe_lookups so support can triage.

Jin (sdk): Agreed. Short-term: recommend customers set header 'stream-session-id: <uuid>' and we'll implement a dedupe layer for 1 minute on the backend. Long-term: SDK fix will (1) make aclose() reliable, (2) propagate EOF as an explicit 'event: done' when TCP close is observed, and (3) retry logic will coordinate with iterator state machine instead of racing.

Mona (sre): I've reproduced locally with a test harness that injects a TCP FIN before the final SSE event. Repro steps attached to the issue.

Jin (sdk): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1427 — includes fix for Python async iterator, and an update to Node/TS EventSource wrapper to emit an explicit 'done' event on socket close. Canary scheduled.
